video_title: Cooper Flagg's LIMITLESS Potential & How To Build A Winner With Mavs' President Masai Ujiri

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri on the Mavericks losing Jalen Brunson in free agency
quotes.excerpt: You guys lost Jalen Brunson in free agency. You guys got any picks or anything back?

text_blocks.speaker: Masai Ujiri
text_blocks.text: You guys lost Jalen Brunson in free agency. You guys got any picks or anything back?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: No, we had to send picks to get rid of him. Are you kidding me? That was a salary dump.

quotes.speaker: Masai Ujiri
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri on the challenges of building a winning NBA team
quotes.excerpt: We are blessed that there are only 30 of these jobs, and every team is different.
quotes.quote: All situations are really different. Obviously, you start from the top, you start from ownership, and then you trickle down. You think about the city, you think about the fans, you think about the current roster. You look at everything. That is true due diligence. We are blessed that there are only 30 of these jobs, and every team is different. When these jobs are open, there is a reason why they are open. I don't think anybody is in a hurry to take this job. There is no opening in this team, the ones that are easy, so you have to look at it that way.

quotes.speaker: Masai Ujiri
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri on the maturity and potential of Cooper Flagg
quotes.excerpt: For a 19-year-old, the maturity, the talent, the character, it's incredible.
quotes.quote: For a 19-year-old, the maturity, the talent, the character, it's incredible. I went to his home in Maine for his camps, and just seeing where he comes from and what that means to him, value, it's something incredible to see. Just the combination of all, we wish he goes with good health and guidance, but he is one of those generational talents. I see it every day, I see it in the gym, and you are like, wow, look at this guy. And that is why to your second question, we have to play good basketball.

quotes.speaker: Masai Ujiri
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri on the league-wide awareness of Cooper Flagg's talent
quotes.excerpt: All 29 other teams know this player. There's nobody that doesn't.
quotes.quote: I don't follow as much from a media standpoint, but I know what I see every day. And I know the people that have scouted and know, they know the player. All 29 other teams know this player. There's nobody that doesn't. And for me, we are going to do everything to put him in position to succeed in this league. There's no question about that, and I see him, how you see him, 100 times even more, because we have the ability to see it every day.

quotes.speaker: Masai Ujiri
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri on the unique talent of Kyrie Irving
quotes.excerpt: I think it was Kevin Durant that said it, there's only one Kyrie walking around in the world.
quotes.quote: I think it was Kevin Durant that said it, there's only one Kyrie walking around in the world. It's crazy that you see him too and his talent. And that's kind of what we see, even if it's to ease up the game. But also Kyrie as a player, we truly believe in him, we truly believe that he can succeed on our team. This is not why just, I truly believe that if we have the right players playing, we can really grow as a team in a new system with a new culture that we are trying to build.

quotes.speaker: Masai Ujiri
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri on the difficulty of trading and losing players
quotes.excerpt: There's two things that are really tough in our league: trading a player and when a player leaves.
quotes.quote: There's two things that are really tough in our league: trading a player and when a player leaves. And if I have the ability or I have, in my job, I trade DeMar DeRozan or Pascal Siakam, it kills me. That's a part of the business I hate. Who am I to question if Kawhi leaves? And that's the way I really looked at it, honestly. If he chose, face-to-face, he told me he wanted to go home, and he wanted to go back. Forget all the other outside stuff. If he looks at me eye-to-eye and with our friendship, families, I'm not going to doubt that.

quotes.speaker: Carlos Boozer
quotes.summary_phrase: Carlos Boozer on playing for Jerry Sloan in Utah
quotes.excerpt: Jerry is as old school, throwback of a coach as you can get.
quotes.quote: For me it was awesome. Jerry is as old school, throwback of a coach as you can get. People talk about Tom Thibodeau and the Van Gundys and Pat, Phil Jackson, like Jerry was cut from that same cloth. I remember seeing an interview that Jerry West did, and they asked him like who was his toughest opponent. And I have all these guys in my mind that I think he's going to say, and he goes Jerry Sloan. And he said because every time I ever played against Jerry Sloan, I felt like I was in a war.

quotes.speaker: Carlos Boozer
quotes.summary_phrase: Carlos Boozer on the current state of the Utah Jazz
quotes.excerpt: You see some of the moves that Austin has made since he came over last summer.
quotes.quote: You see some of the moves that Austin has made since he came over last summer. Getting Triple J was a huge move. Jaren Jackson Jr. is a stud on both sides of the ball. Keeping Lauri Markkanen in place, taking care of Keyonte George who had a breakout year I thought last year despite the wins and losses. Obviously, posturing to get the number one pick and they ended up getting Darren Peterson, which is a phenomenal, phenomenal pick. And you guys have seen what he can bring to the table and he's only 19, 20 years old, has a bright future ahead of him.

quotes.speaker: Carlos Boozer
quotes.summary_phrase: Carlos Boozer on Will Hardy's coaching style
quotes.excerpt: Will Hardy is a phenomenal coach. He has an incredible background, he has a terrific mind.
quotes.quote: Will Hardy is a phenomenal coach. He has an incredible background, he has a terrific mind for the game and he's still so young enough to be connected to all the players. He has that young, enthusiastic ability to teach the younger generation. And if these guys can defend, you guys know how the West is, there's no joke. If they can defend at a high level and that they can find a way to share the ball offensively, they I think they have enough scorers to score with most of the teams.
